notes: v2.5.14 - required update. Quality & AS9100: the Risk module has been rebuilt to the specification the quality team asked for. Risks are now scored on Severity and Frequency on a 1-25 scale, with Frequency optional, and Detection and RPN have been removed. Categories, source/trigger and current control are pick-lists of real, plain-English options instead of free text, only a category and a description are required to raise a risk, and there is now one badge scan instead of two. Every existing risk has been re-banded onto the new scale; nothing has been deleted. Inventory: Physical Inventory is split into three tabs - project stock, consumables and unclassified - with a proper worklist for stock nobody has classified yet, consumables shown as the received lots they actually are with readable names, and columns that now stay blank rather than state a figure they cannot know. Each lot carries its own editable Lot Description alongside the read-only Part Description, and both are searchable. Sourcing & Stock - the quantities now match the shelf: on-hand on the materials list is a real calculated figure instead of zero, available versus allocated is worked out from genuine commitments so fully-spoken-for material stops appearing available, shortages count what has already been consumed instead of raising phantom shortfalls, and stock that arrived before a vendor part was linked to a material is adopted the moment the link is made. Receiving can now point a part at a material that already exists or create a project material rather than only creating something new, the unclassified-parts backlog is on the dashboard, material names follow one rule everywhere, and the Vendor Parts tab leads through to the part instead of being a dead end. Purchasing: the vendor picker is 851 names shorter - vendors with no order, requisition or receipt since 2020 have been retired from the pickers, taking the selectable list from 2,065 to 1,214. Nothing historical changes and any of them can be reinstated. CATIA remote viewing: a machine is now released however the session ends - a crash, a power cut, quitting the app or closing the stream window - not only when you press Disconnect, and abandoned queue places are cleared, so machines stop reading as permanently claimed while nobody is on them. Waiting in the queue no longer looks like a disconnection. The stream window closes properly, full screen genuinely fills the screen with no second taskbar, CATIA no longer fights you for the mouse and keyboard, the remote machines have an orange taskbar so you always know which desktop you are looking at, the session controls have moved off the video and into the AOS streaming panel, you can pick which machine to connect to and queue for that specific machine, and copy and paste works in both directions. Workforce planner: every build that is in progress now appears, including builds with no hours budgeted, hovering a build shows its hours, dates, schedule position and department problems, departments over capacity or out of window are flagged on the build itself, the build hours screen is a compact table, a department with no capacity recorded reads as "no data" instead of a crisis, and the page no longer dims every few minutes while you are reading it. Project hours accuracy: time now follows the job code people clock into, so hours land on the project the work was actually done for rather than being credited to the wrong one - some projects will show hours that were previously credited elsewhere or not showing at all. Access: creating and editing materials and vendor-part links is now limited to the people who do that work; shop-floor actions - adjusting, consuming, outlife and splitting - are deliberately unchanged for everyone. Also: the retired Project Tracker page has been removed, Inventory's pop-ups all share one consistent look, and there are various fixes to project date handling and hours reporting. Workforce planner - recording hours a department still needs: you can now record extra hours a department needs after its budget is used up. Until now, once a department had worked through the hours budgeted for it there was nowhere to say it still had work left to do, so a department that had burned everything it was given read as free and the planner kept handing it more work. The only thing you have to enter is the number of hours - a reason, dates, confidence and a link to the NCR or ticket behind it are all optional - and the form states what it is about to do before you commit it. It takes two clicks to reach: an "Add hours" action on each department row in the build hover panel, and a + on each row of the Department Hours table. Added hours are shown separately from the budget and never mixed into it, they count in the forecast so a department that has burned its budget but still has work in front of it reads as loaded rather than free, and they appear on the Project Details schedule, the burndown, the Analytics tab and in the CSV, HTML and diagnostics exports. A block with no dates on it says so rather than being drawn somewhere it does not belong, and any block can be withdrawn without erasing the record of it. Build problems now show on the project list itself: a build with a department over capacity, past the end of its window, or working with no budget at all says so on its own row, in words, instead of looking clean until somebody opened it - and where the information to judge a department was not available the row stays silent rather than claiming a clean bill of health. Copy and paste between your PC and the CATIA machine now works properly in both directions, including large copies that previously looked like they had worked and then pasted nothing at all. Reporting accuracy: overtime percentages in department reporting were overstated because the percentage counted double time as overtime while the hours column beside it did not - both now use one definition and double time is reported alongside as its own figure, so the corrected percentages are lower than what was shown before for every department that books double time. A project 19 days past its date with 1,303 hours still to do was reading as 100% likely to finish on time, because the calculation could not tell "there is nothing left to do" apart from "there are no days left to do it in"; those are now two different answers. Added hours are no longer drawn as the budget slipping, and remaining work is no longer floored at zero on the Analytics tab, which had made an overrun look like a finished job. This release also updates the database behind AOS, so please update as soon as you are prompted.
